prediction_target.context: designated entity occurrences at their supplied offsets in the original sentence

native_label_definitions.no_relation: No evaluated chemical-protein relation is expressed for the designated pair. Other relation types and co-occurrence alone belong here.
native_label_definitions.CPR:3: UPREGULATOR / ACTIVATOR: increased target activity or expression, including indirect positive regulation.
native_label_definitions.CPR:4: DOWNREGULATOR / INHIBITOR: decreased target activity or expression, including indirect negative regulation.
native_label_definitions.CPR:5: AGONIST / AGONIST-ACTIVATOR / AGONIST-INHIBITOR: an agonist relation to the target receptor.
native_label_definitions.CPR:9: SUBSTRATE / PRODUCT OF: the chemical is a substrate, substrate/product, or product of the protein.

annotation_rules.text: Classify the designated chemical and gene/protein mentions at their supplied positions. Interpret abbreviations, apposition and coordination in the sentence. A relation of different participants, co-occurrence alone, or an unevaluated relation type does not establish an evaluated relation for this pair.

Relations may be explicit or implicit in the whole sentence, including biochemical interpretation. Absence of a literal category word does not by itself exclude a relation. The inference must be supported by the supplied text, not merely by a known association between the entities.

A chemical mention that occurs only inside a protein name does not receive a substrate/product relation to that protein, including when the target protein is its abbreviation. A separate mention of the same chemical is a different candidate and requires its own sentence-supported relation. Do not transfer its relation to the name-internal mention.

CPR:9 covers substrate, product, or both. Substrate includes a reactant acted on in an enzyme-mediated reaction and a transporter substrate; product includes an enzymatic-reaction or transporter product. Interpret process roles; the words substrate or product need not appear. Mere association is insufficient.
CPR:3 and CPR:4 include increased or decreased target activity or expression, respectively, whether direct or indirect. Do not require direct physical binding for these regulation classes.

CPR:6 is the expressed antagonist assignment. Interpret relationship-bearing noun phrases, their named members, and target abbreviations in context. Distinguish antagonism from agonism and from other negative regulation.
